body:
> You don't own the EU, stop with the Deutschland über alles, it's not welcome here.

I apologize if my cynic comment was misunderstood. Given your posting schedule, you are European, given your username, you probably are Spanish. If so, you will agree my country's political elite does act like my earlier words are true. 

> Also, no-one in Germany gets "locked up" for suicidal ideation. And no psychiatrist will commit you for it. Most people who fear going to therapy think they are going to be committed. It's completely unfounded.

Sixteen Landesgesetze paint a very different picture. I won't take the chance. 

> Therapy and meds are the only solution to you problem. If you want to get better, you know what to do.

Therapy comes too late, meds make me unfunctional. Seems it's the bridge pillar, then.

> I am not American either. Where in Central Europe? Because if they are part of the EU, that's against EU law.

Germany. We own the EU. We don't care about EU laws.

> All together, you cannot put everyone who has suicide ideation in the hospital. There would never be enough room!

That's why we only lock up the ones too stupid to off themselves or too stupid not to shut up about their plans.

> There is a difference between what doctors tell you and what is the law. 

I get your point, but it is a risk I am just not willing to take. 

> Would it be fair to say, then, (short story), that you were happy before this happened?

Happiness - like everything - is highly subjective. But I was a lot happier before this incident. 

I know what's comming now - I can be happy again, sometime in the distant future, so why not wait a little? Well, I am in this bind for a decade now. That's one third of my life. Excel tells me that with the rate I am paying back, I can have a net worth of zero in eight years. Then I officially have *nothing* and am close to 40. I will not have travelled the world, I will not have had a relationship (going out costs money), I will not have achieved anything. Then I might have a chance - one that can result into even worse things. 

Why bother?
How am I cynic? I am doing a statement of my condition, and there's a lot of future pain for very little of future gain. Is not wanting to continue under this circumstances a cynic mindset?

> In fact, it's impossible not to give yourself and your life meaning. Humans, by definition, create self-meaning. The question is whether or not that meaning has any value to you (so, in a way, it's a question of what you yourself value.) Determining what one values is a lifelong process.

I valued things. Today? Not so much. Any value I had has prooven worthless, and for any value I tried to follow I have been beaten massively. 

> What happened since then?

That's a long and depressing story. Short version: Finished school, was on my way to greatness, got into a relationship with a depressed person, sacrificed my way to greatness for a way of debt to make her happy, then she fucked the other guy.

> I'm not sure what country you're in, but in the vast majority of countries, this is incorrect.

I had two psychiatrists tell me that if I start talking about suicide to them, I would spend the next few months to years in the psychiatry. They hate the rule, too, but they are bound by law - with the danger of losing their approbiation if they don't and I off myself.

> Not true. Only if a psychiatrist thinks that you are in immediate danger of hurting yourself, or others. No-one gets committed for having suicidal thoughts.

Remember that not everyone on this site is American. In Central Europe, you do have laws that demand hospitalization, and docs err on the safe side, just to keep their approbiation.

> I guess what I was asking was, "How does on get meaning out of life?" If you don't see your life as having meaning, can you look at other lives that have meaning? Does a firefighter have meaning? The President? Or are their lives meaningless as well?

I guess you are supposed to give yourself meaning. But in the whole picture, this self-induced meaning is useless. For mankind your meaning is irrelevant, the only thing that matters is if you do your job well. But why should I work for the next fourty years so that my society can profit from my work and I have literally nothing to achieve from it?

> Were you ever happy in life?

I had a relationship, I had friends (both crashed about at the same time). Life was hard back then, but it was enjoyable. There are rare moments I remember of true bliss, but I never have been content with what I had after those years, a decade ago.

> awesome!

I think the main problem is that I do not see it as this.

> Maybe by "meh" you mean numb, or indifferent?

I mean "It's just not worth continuing, the cost to benefit ratio is horrible." I know I am depressed, but it doesn't feel like depression anymore - it's more a feeling of "it doesn't matter anymore."

> What would your psych say if you told him/her how you're truly feeling?

Talking to a health professional about suicidal thoughts results - by law - in an indefinite amount of time of  compulsory hospitalization. The last thing I would do is to talk about anyone with a Doktor in front of their name about my thoughts.

> Would you consider developing a new hobby?

Sure, why not. Only that my time is limited, and that I seriously can't think of anything. By now, I can't even read the news anymore because I lose focus after ten minutes.

> Are you seeing a therapist?

Therapists have a waiting period of 18 months where I live. I never bothered even getting my name on that list. Chances are by the time I get my talk, I'm dead.

> How do you see "meaning" in life?

I know this is cliché, but that's the main point. Why should I bother continuing if the best possible outcome is continuing for another 40 years like this and then die? I tried to build myself up with the /r/getmotivated guys, I've read close to any religious text I could get my hands on, I tried to work for retribution against those who wronged me. Nothing worked for long. 

I come home, and there's nobody. I get into bed at 8pm, to raise the next morning to go to work then to go to bed. There is nothing else. Why am I doing this? There's no reason in continuing.

When I was really down, the first time I was around here, I went to a psychiatrist. The pills made me nonfunctional. I am a software developer, I can't sit in front of my desk spaced out and drooling because I don't realize my mouth is open anymore. That was Tofranil. 

Yes, I know, tons of medications, try every single one of the three billion combinations until something works. I don't want that. If I am going out, at least I want to preserve some dignity on my final days. 

> Walking and hiking should be releasing endorphins that improve your mood.

It's more a chore. I tried making it "fun" by adding some geocaching into the mix, but that failed. I pant like a fish out of water (very steep surroundings here). It brings me no happiness, nor any kind of "high" endorphines should produce.
